## Specific task description

Task instruction: Put a pair of the synthetic shoe upper in the rectangular Nike box for shoes, tips pointing left.

Task description: Place the pair of red shoes, currently on opposite sides of the table, into the open orange rectangular Nike shoe box in front. Both toes should point toward the left side of the head-camera view.

Success criteria: Place the left shoe in the front-central box region (lower in the image), and the right shoe in the rear-central region (upper in the image), lowering both to the box bottom. Both must lie flat, soles down and toes left in the image, with both grippers open.

## Execution tips

- Select a narrower, accessible middle section of the shoe and grasp across its width. Contact flat sides near the white sole's upper edge, with a small opening margin beyond local width, reducing slippage from gripping the tongue, laces or curved toe.
- Before closing, confirm the fingers are actually on opposite shoe sides with sufficient pad contact. Use a small test lift to check stable movement with the gripper, avoiding a grasp that only overlaps in the image.
- The left shoe already points roughly left, so its orientation can be retained. The right shoe requires a larger turn. Adjust in open space with its sole above the box rim, away from the rear-right carton and mallet, allowing clearance for the toe's sweep.
- When lowering into the box, leave clearance between the shoe toe, heel, and gripper fingers and the box walls. Also watch the other shoe to avoid pushing, rotating, or catching it on the rim.
- Once the sole is supported by the box bottom, open slowly, watching whether the spreading fingers touch the box wall or other shoe. Withdraw upward where possible to reduce dropping on release or dragging the shoe out of alignment.
